title: Image UMAP: real measurements and interactive crop inspection
description: Build a bounded embedding from the downloaded example measurements, inspect real crops interactively and locate the nested projection tools.
objectives: Reuse the downloaded project and select its measurement tables.
Configure a small reproducible embedding and inspect its preprocessing and outputs.
Click fitted points to inspect their actual crops without changing annotations.
Find nested Image Scatter and PCA, search controls, optional acceleration and AI assistance.
prerequisite: Use Annotate's Load test data route first to obtain the 2,341 PNG crops and measurements database. Image UMAP reuses that project; it does not download another dataset in this recording. The example uses measured features on CPU, not neural image features.

scenes.narration: Open Image UMAP from the Home screen's Tools section. It places objects using their measured features, then lets you inspect the corresponding microscopy crops. A nearby group on this exploratory map is not automatically a biological class.

Reuse the project downloaded through Annotate's Load test data route. It contains two thousand three hundred and forty-one crops and their measurements database. Follow the linked Annotate lesson for the actual download; this module now opens the existing project.

Source uses Add project folders. Select the plate folder, not an individual image. The control reports the databases, rows and shared columns before merging. When comparing several projects, inspect source-related structure before interpreting a cluster as biology.

Choose the measurement tables that define the question. This example uses cell, cytoplasm, nucleus and pathogen measurements. Review missing data and correlated-feature removal. Leave Resnet features off: raw-crop neural embeddings are not implemented by this route.

Set Row limit to four hundred for a small demonstration. This caps the sampled objects; it does not make the sample representative of every experiment. Two workers keep the job bounded, and the original database remains available for a larger analysis.

Reduction method selects UMAP here. The current form also offers other reducers, with their own controls. A PCA or t-SNE setting is not interchangeable with a UMAP setting. Only UMAP was fitted in this demonstration.

We use fifteen neighbours and a minimum distance of zero point one. Neighbourhood size affects how local structure is represented; minimum distance affects how tightly points can pack. These are demonstration choices, not universally optimal biological settings.

Keep the reducer seed at forty-two when comparing the same inputs. The seeded CPU implementation may use one thread for reproducibility even when more workers are requested. A seed does not make different feature selections or different backends equivalent.

Clustering is separate from dimensionality reduction. This DBSCAN example assigns all four hundred objects to cluster zero, and we keep noise removal off. That single label is a computed grouping, not a finding that all cells share one phenotype.

Enable crop images and points together. Twelve small crop glyphs make the static map inspectable without covering the point cloud. Display choices help you read the result; they do not replace reviewing the features that produced its geometry.

Press Run and read the real console. This run reports median imputation of missing measurements and a four-hundred-by-two embedding. Inspect those preprocessing decisions, not just the Finished mark. No image segmentation or classifier training occurred here.

Inspect the saved embedding figure and the results folder. The exported table contains the selected measurement rows, metadata and cluster labels. Do not assume that this build also exports the two plotted coordinates into that table.

Turn on Interactive to explore the already fitted map. This is not a live refit of changing settings. Clicking points, zooming and selecting regions helps inspect the current result; changing the analysis still requires another run.

Click a point and inspect its actual crop at the right. The displayed path ties the image to its source object. Here the crop was loaded by the real application after the click, not substituted with a representative image.

Click another point to compare its morphology. The sidebar also offers selection labelling and automatic-cluster propagation. Those actions write annotations, unlike simply viewing a crop. We did not press them, and verified that the database remained unchanged.

Image Scatter and PCA now sit in Image UMAP's header. Use Image Scatter for direct feature relationships and PCA for a linear projection and its loadings. Their existing specialist lessons remain linked under this parent module.

Hyperparameter search opens a separate comparison panel. Keep any search small and inspect the resulting layouts before propagating settings. This recording shows the actual controls only; no search was started and no chosen result was invented.

The GPU control is optional. This recording used CPU. Supported reducers can use the optional RAPIDS backend when it is available; that is a different acceleration path from Torch's device selection. Read the reported backend and do not promise identical coordinates across devices.

AI enables optional provider assistance, not automatic biological interpretation. This question was not sent. For scripts, the corresponding entry point is generate_image_umap in spacr.core; keep the input tables, preprocessing and saved settings with the resulting figure.
